header_title: The Force That Should Tear You Apart
question_text: If electric forces are 10^36 times stronger than gravity, why don't you fly apart?
audio_script: Here is a puzzle. Electric forces are ten to the thirty-sixth times stronger than gravity. Every proton in your body repels every other proton with a force that should launch you into space. Yet you sit still. Why? The answer is the finest cancellation in nature. Every electron pulls back with almost exactly the same force. The imbalance is less than one part in ten to the twenty-five. If it were one percent, you would lift the Earth. But it is not. So the next time you sit in a chair, remember: you are held together by the most precise balance in the universe.

question_text: What single equation describes every motor
audio_script: ["\\vec{F} = q(\\vec{E} + \\vec{v} \\times \\vec{B})"]
beats_json: Every force in electromagnetism comes from one line. The force on a charge is q times E plus q times v cross B. Electric field pushes along. Magnetic field pushes sideways, always perpendicular to motion. Change the sign of the charge and the push flips. That is it. Maxwell's equations tell the fields where to be. Lorentz tells the charges how to move. Between them, they explain radio, radar, X-rays, and the glow of a plasma. One equation. Everything.

tagline: Why two charges can cancel to zero
question_text: Where is the electric field exactly zero between two equal charges?
audio_script: Two equal positive charges sit on a line. Between them, each pushes the other way. At the exact midpoint, the two pushes are equal and opposite. The field is zero. But notice what is not zero: the field elsewhere. Off the axis, the arrows do not cancel. This is superposition in action. You solve one charge at a time, then add the arrows. The zero is not an accident. It is a structural consequence of symmetry, and it is the same reason a soap film is flat in the middle of a frame.

tagline: Why magnetism is just electricity in disguise
question_text: If you run alongside a current-carrying wire

orientation: Here is a secret that took relativity to uncover. Magnetism is not a separate force. It is electricity seen from a moving frame. Two protons side by side repel electrically. Run alongside them at their speed. They are at rest. Pure electric. In your frame there is a magnetic field. In theirs, there is none. So is magnetism real? It is a relativistic correction. In a wire, electrons drift at a tenth of a millimetre per second. v squared over c squared is ten to the minus twenty-five. But the electric force has cancelled to better than that. Only the tiny leftover remains. That leftover moves motors and paints the aurora.

header_title: The Gap That Made Light Possible
question_text: What did Maxwell add to Ampere's law to make light possible?
audio_script: Ampere's law works beautifully for steady currents. Then Maxwell noticed a flaw. Charge a capacitor. Current flows in the wires, stops at the gap. Draw a surface across the wire. Current passes through. Draw it through the gap. No current. Same loop, two answers. Something is missing. Maxwell proposed that a changing electric field is itself a current. Add that displacement current and the loop works everywhere. The universe works. Without this fix, no light could travel through empty space.

question_text: How do you measure the electric field without touching it?
audio_script: Imagine the electric field as water flowing outward from a charge. Draw a closed surface around it. Count how much water crosses per second. That is the flux. If the charge is inside, the flux is the same no matter the surface. Tiny sphere, lumpy bag, giant cube. Same answer. If the charge is outside, whatever flows in flows out. Net zero. This single rule is Coulomb's inverse square restated. It is the reason you can solve problems without integrating.

question_text: How do you measure how much a field circles a loop?
audio_script: Freeze a fluid. Cut a thin tube through it along a closed loop. Inside, the liquid keeps circulating. The momentum is trapped. Speed times circumference is circulation. For a magnetic field around a wire, the same idea applies. Walk a closed curve. Dot each B with the step forward. Sum them up. That number tells you how much current threads your loop. That is Ampere's law. The magnetic twin of Gauss's law.

tagline: Why electrons don't crash into the nucleus
question_text: If opposites attract

orientation: Common sense says electrons should spiral into protons. They attract. They are close. Nothing stops them. But they do not. Quantum mechanics does. Squeeze an electron into a tiny region and the uncertainty principle gives it enormous momentum. A wild jitter that fights the attraction. Balance the two and you get a stable atom. The electron sits at the distance where electric pull equals quantum push. Remove the wobble and matter collapses in a flash. The universe is held up by uncertainty.

header_title: The Map Is Not the Territory
tagline: Why field lines are a lie
question_text: What is wrong with drawing electric field lines?
audio_script: For a century physicists drew field lines. Arrows from positive to negative. Denser where the field is strong. Beautiful. Then relativity arrived. Ride along with a magnet at light speed. Its B field disappears. Lines cannot disappear. They are not real. Neither are they useless. The field is the thing. A mathematical object at every point. Whether or not anyone draws it. Field lines are shadows on the wall. Useful for intuition. Dangerous for the soul.

tagline: How a tiny imbalance could lift the Earth
question_text: What if you had just one percent more electrons than protons?
audio_script: One percent. That is all. If you and a friend each carried one percent more electrons than protons, the repulsion would be enough to lift the Earth. Not a building. Not a mountain. The planet. The electric force is that strong. Yet we feel nothing. Because every proton pull cancels every electron push to one part in ten to the twenty-five. The leftover is what holds your chair together. And what keeps you from exploding.

header_title: Estimate the Force of a One Percent Imbalance
question_text: Two 70 kg people stand 1 m apart. Each has 1% more electrons than protons. Roughly how large is the repulsive force?
audio_script: Let us reason like Feynman. First, count the protons. Seventy kilograms of water is about seven times ten to the twenty-eight nucleons. One percent is seven times ten to the twenty-six charges. Multiply by 1.6 times ten to the minus nineteen coulombs. You get about ten to the seventh coulombs on each body. Now Coulomb. k is nine times ten to the ninth. q squared is ten to the fourteenth. r squared is one. The force is ten to the twenty-fifth newtons. That is the weight of the Earth. Two people. One metre apart. The electric force you never feel.

question_text: Two protons are 10^-15 m apart. How many times stronger is the electric repulsion than gravity?
audio_script: Both forces go as one over r squared. The distance cancels. So the ratio is a pure number. Electric strength divided by gravitational strength. Electric: k e squared. Nine times ten to the ninth, times 1.6 times ten to the minus nineteen, squared. About 2.3 times ten to the minus twenty-eight. Gravitational: G m squared. Six point seven times ten to the minus eleven, times 1.67 times ten to the minus twenty-seven, squared. About 1.9 times ten to the minus sixty-four. Divide. Ten to the thirty-six. The reason you neither fly apart nor collapse.

tagline: Putting the Lorentz force to work
question_text: A proton moves at 3×10^6 m/s along +x. E = 2×10^5 V/m along +y. B = 0.5 T along +z. What is the net force?
audio_script: Compute each piece separately. Electric force: q E. Proton charge is 1.6 times ten to the minus nineteen. E is two times ten to the fifth. That gives 3.2 times ten to the minus fourteen newtons in the plus y direction. Magnetic piece: q v cross B. v is three times ten to the sixth in x. B is one half in z. Cross product is minus 1.5 times ten to the sixth in y. Multiply by q: minus 2.4 times ten to the minus thirteen newtons in y. Add them. The electric push is tiny. The magnetic push dominates. Net is about 2.1 times ten to the minus thirteen newtons in minus y.

question_text: Two +q charges sit at x = -a and x = +a. What is the field at x = 0 and x = 3a?
audio_script: At the midpoint, each charge pushes with equal strength in opposite directions. Net is exactly zero. Now go to x equals three a. That is two a from the right charge, four a from the left. Field from the right: k q over four a squared, pointing toward plus x. Field from the left: k q over sixteen a squared, pointing toward minus x. Subtract. Three k q over sixteen a squared, plus x. The field is not one over distance squared from a single point. It is a sum. Superposition is doing the work.

header_title: Flux Through a Surface That Misses the Charge
question_text: A +q charge sits just outside a closed spherical surface. What is the net flux through the surface?
audio_script: Gauss's law: flux through any closed surface equals enclosed charge over epsilon zero. A charge outside the surface? Zero. Why? Every field line that enters must exit. They are not created or destroyed in empty space. Pick a line skimming in. Follow it through. It comes out. Count plus one. Count minus one. Zero. Put the charge inside. Every line that starts on it must end outside. Count of outbound lines equals charge over epsilon zero. The surface shape does not matter. Only what is inside.

header_title: Circulation of B Around a Wire
question_text: A long straight wire carries 2 A. A circular loop of radius 0.5 m circles it. What is the line integral of B around the loop?
audio_script: Ampere's law does not ask you to compute B. It asks for the integral. Epsilon zero c squared is exactly four pi times ten to the minus seven. Multiply by the enclosed current of two amperes. Eight pi times ten to the minus seven. Roughly 2.5 times ten to the minus six tesla metres. The radius does not appear. Any loop surrounding the wire gives the same integral. One metre, one kilometre, tangled, circular. Only when the wire is outside does the answer drop to zero. Ampere's law is a bookkeeping shortcut. How much current threads your loop?

header_title: Which Way Does the Force Point?
question_text: An electron moves east through a magnetic field pointing north. Which direction is the magnetic force?
audio_script: Right-hand rule first. Index finger east. Middle finger north. Thumb points up. That would be the force on a positive charge. But our particle is an electron. Negative. Flip the direction. Down. This is the trap exams love. The rule is for a positive charge. For an electron the force is opposite. So the electron is pushed downward. This is why electrons in a cathode ray tube bend one way while protons bend the other for the same v and B. The arrow from v cross B is what a positive charge would feel.

question_text: Two long parallel wires, 2 A and 4 A in the same direction, 0.1 m apart. What is the force per unit length?
audio_script: Same-direction currents attract. Opposite-direction currents repel. That is the magnetic handshake. Now magnitude. Mu zero times I one I two over two pi d. Mu zero is four pi times ten to the minus seven. I one times I two is eight. Two pi d is two pi times 0.1. Cancel pi. Four times ten to the minus seven, times eight, over 0.2. That is 1.6 times ten to the minus five newtons per metre. Small but real. This is how current balances work. The magnetic attraction between coils calibrates the ampere.

question_text: A parallel-plate capacitor of area 0.01 m² is charged at 5 A. What is dE/dt between the plates?
audio_script: Maxwell's displacement current equals epsilon zero times dE/dt times area. That must equal the actual current in the wire. Five amperes. So dE/dt equals I over epsilon zero times area. Five over eight point eight five times ten to the minus twelve, times one hundredth. Five over eight point eight five times ten to the minus fourteen. Roughly five point six five times ten to the thirteen volts per metre per second. Staggering. But required. The changing E between the plates acts like a real current. That is why electromagnetic waves travel in vacuum. E changes create B. B changes create E. No charges needed.

header_title: Why Magnetism Is a Tiny Correction
tagline: The v²/c² in the fine print
question_text: In a copper wire with electron drift speed 0.1 mm/s, what is v²/c²?
audio_script: Drift velocity is a tenth of a millimetre per second. Ten to the minus four metres per second. Square it. Ten to the minus eight. c squared is nine times ten to the sixteen. Divide. About ten to the minus twenty-five. Absurdly small. So why does magnetism matter? Because the electric field between moving electrons in two parallel wires is enormous. But it almost perfectly cancels the proton field. The cancellation is good to far better than ten to the minus twenty-five. Only the tiny leftover remains. That leftover is magnetism. Magnetic force is the relativistic tail of an almost perfect balance.
